messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of GPUs in europe1-row7 show repeated power-limit events + thermal climb, started ~06:40 UTC. Affected 4 cards on host gw-r7-03. Inference tail p95 jumped to 1.8s from 120ms.
ashwin: ugh. any Xid codes in dmesg?
maria: yes, logs show a couple Xid 13 and Xid 61 around the same time. nv-host log attached (snippet):
```
[2026-03-18T06:40:03Z] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 61
[2026-03-18T06:40:03Z] GPU 0: Power limit reached, throttling
[2026-03-18T06:40:04Z] temp: GPU 0 sensor 92C
```
kyle: good catch. oncall-bot, where are the recent powercap changes? any firmware pushes?
oncall-bot: No scheduled firmware jobs in europe1 this week. Last power policy change on gw-r7-03: none.
jess: are we sure it's a hardware thermal/power issue vs a sudden load pattern? logs + duty cycles look consistent with thermal climb not sustained load burst.
maria: load hasn't increased, same request qps. KV cache miss rate unchanged. Batching slightly higher but not enough to explain 92C.
ashwin: can you run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,power.draw,clocks.sm --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-sample.csv` and paste last 30s? Also `ipmitool sdr` for PSU rails.
maria: pasted output to thread. quick summary: one 12V rail sag on host, PSU temp warnings at 63C, fans at 80% but one fan tach fluctuating between 15k and 22k rpm.
kyle: sounds like localized cooling loss causing powercap to kick. Recommendation: drain the host and swap the PSU / fan assembly, mark host DRAINING to scheduler.
jess: agree. also pin inference fallbacks to other region before drain — route heavy queries to dedicated in us-central for latency-sensitive customers. Can we do a rolling drain? we need 2 spare cards in europe to handle load or we risk throttling elsewhere.
maria: starting soft drain now: cordon host, drain long-running pods. will keep 4 GPU jobs running for graceful handoff for 5m.
maria: command run: `kubectl cordon gw-r7-03 && kubectl drain gw-r7-03 --ignore-daemonsets --grace-period=300`
ashwin: while that's happening, let's temporarily lower power limit on affected cards to safe value to avoid trips: `nvidia-smi -i 0 -pl 250` (was 300W). only as stopgap. Note: we should be careful with power limits and warranty.
kyle: open a hardware ticket with vendor, include Xid logs + PSU sensor dump. I've created HW-4521 and assigned to vendor-support.
maria: created infra incident: INF-2026-117, added oncall and hw ticket links. routing change in progress: traffic for route /model/realtime/* -> fallback cluster queued.
jess: monitoring: set up short-term alert to escalate if p95 > 500ms or GPU temp > 85C on any host. Also add a dashboard panel for per-host fan tach variance.
maria: post-repro notes: swapping PSU + fan bracket fixed temp curve in lab. will schedule a hot-swap for gw-r7-03 today 10:00 UTC.
nashwin: action items: 1) drain+replace PSU/fan, 2) vendor ticket HW-4521, 3) temp/p95 alert runbook updated, 4) add automated cordon when powercap > 3 events in 5m, 5) follow-up on potential firmware reflash if vendor recommends.
kyle: one more: check ECC counters post-swap and run a stress test (30m) with telemetry capture.
maria: logging steps in INF-2026-117, will post postmortem if root cause confirmed. thanks all :thumbsup:
